Notes are in /Users/ruhaanrajadhyaksha/projects/grok/heracles/paper/litcheck/items/f4-margin-peaks/CHECK.md.

(0) Internal problem. sections/experiments.tex holds only TODO comments, and groups.tex is a skeleton. Nothing in the paper supports "normalized margin peaks at the predicted optimum", so this empirical claim in the abstract is currently unsupported.

(1) Morwani et al., fetched from arxiv.org/html/2311.07568.
- Fig 1(c): "For the quadratic activation, the network asymptotically reaches the maximum L_{2,3} margin predicted by our analysis" (mod-71, trained with L_{2,3} regularisation).
- Fig 6(a) says the same for S_5, and Fig 5 for sparse parity with L_{2,5}.
- Our Cor. dense (approach.tex l.69-71) reproduces their value, sqrt(2/27)/(p^{1/2}(p-1)).
- So "matching Morwani for their case" holds as a formula match. But Morwani shows convergence over training, not a peak over feature count.

(2) Chughtai, Chan, Nanda, ICML 2023, PMLR 202:6243-6267. Fetched the PMLR page and arxiv.org/html/2302.03025v2.
- Setup: one-hidden-layer ReLU MLP and a transformer, AdamW, weight decay 1, 40% training data. This is not our network class.
- S_5, Fig 7 caption (50 MLP seeds): "Most commonly we have two key representations (typically sign and standard), but sometimes we learn more."
- S_5, Table 5 (MLP): {sign,std-sign,std,5d-a}, {sign,std}, {sign,std,5d-b}, {sign,std}.
- S_5, Table 6 (transformer): {sign,std-sign} x2, {sign,std} x2.
- So "one faithful irrep plus sign" is the most common outcome, not the universal one.
- A_5, Table 5 (MLP): every seed contains the 4d standard irrep as well as 3d-a/3d-b, sometimes also 5d-a. The Galois pair alone appears in 0/4 MLP seeds.
- A_5, Table 6 (transformer): the Galois pair alone appears in 2/4 seeds ({3d-a,3d-b} x2), plus one {5d-a,3d-b,3d-a} and one {std}.
- Sec 6: "the network preferred the standard representation over the standard_sign representation, when in fact standard_sign offers better performance for fixed weight norm." This counts against any claim that the norm ceiling picks which irrep; it can only support the count.
- C_113 MLP (Table 5) uses 10-15 key frequencies. The transformer (Table 6) uses 3-4.

Searches: arXiv HTML full-text extraction of 2302.03025 and 2311.07568; the PMLR page for Chughtai.

recommended_citations.why: S_5 claim: the most common outcome is sign plus one 4d faithful irrep (Fig 7, Tables 5-6). For A_5, the Galois 3d pair appears in most runs, but the MLPs also carry the 4d standard irrep. Cite as the source that is consistent on S_5 and only partly consistent on A_5.

Fig 1(c) and Fig 6(a): trained quadratic nets with L_{2,3} regularisation reach the predicted maximum L_{2,3} margin on mod-71 and S_5. This supports 'matching Morwani for their case' together with our Cor. dense formula.

recommended_change:
Abstract l.58: keep "peaks at the predicted optimum" only once experiments.tex contains a plot of margin against K (or against b) that shows the peak. Otherwise write: "trained networks approach the predicted margin ceiling, recovering the maximum L_{2,3} margin of Morwani et al. at the dense endpoint (b=nu), and the predicted feature count on S_5 (one faithful irrep plus the sign character) agrees with the most common outcome reported by Chughtai et al."

groups.tex: change "one representation on S_5 and the Galois-conjugate pair on A_5, as observed" to cite chughtai2023toy (Fig 7, Tables 5-6) and say "most commonly". For A_5, either credit the Galois pair to our own runs, or note that Chughtai's MLPs also learn the 4d standard irrep (their transformers learn the pair alone in 2/4 seeds). State that the ceiling predicts the count, not which irrep: Chughtai observe the standard irrep preferred over standard_sign even though standard_sign is norm-better. Do not claim the cyclic optimum is consistent with Chughtai, whose ReLU MLPs use 10-15 frequencies at p=113.
